claims.text: Market failure is the failure of the price mechanism, left to itself, to allocate resources in the way that best serves society: some goods are produced at levels above what their full effects on others justify, and others at levels below what those effects warrant.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A private cost is a cost the decision-maker pays directly; an external cost is a cost the activity imposes on people outside the transaction, who receive no payment for it; a social cost is the two combined, the full cost of the activity to society.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A private benefit is a benefit that lands on the buyer; an external benefit is a benefit that lands on people outside the transaction; a social benefit is the two combined, the full benefit of the activity to society.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A public good is a good whose benefits people cannot be stopped from using once it exists, and whose use by one person leaves as much for the next; because those who pay nothing still benefit, private providers tend to withdraw and the market under-provides it.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A merit good, such as schooling or vaccination, is one whose benefits consumers tend to undervalue, so the market under-consumes it; a demerit good, such as tobacco or strong drink, is one whose harm consumers tend to undercount, so the market over-consumes it.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Market failure is sometimes confused with business failure: business failure is one firm closing because it cannot cover its costs, whereas market failure is a whole market settling at the wrong level of output - the test is whether the statement is about a single firm or a whole market.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: The causes of market failure are public goods, merit and demerit goods, external costs, external benefits, the abuse of monopoly power by a single dominant seller, and factor immobility; each leaves some cost or benefit out of the price, so the market settles at a level society would not choose.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Otavi Charcoal Works earns N$40 000 a season burning wood waste, and the smoke it releases over 60 homesteads costs each N$250 a season in cleaning and clinic visits, so 60 x N$250 = N$15 000 a season of costs sit outside the price of charcoal.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A single dominant seller standing behind barriers to entry may hold output below the level a market of many small sellers would produce and keep the price above it, so resources are misallocated towards the seller.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Factor immobility causes market failure when demand shifts between uses: workers fixed to their trade by their skills and to their district by homes and family cannot move at once to where they are needed, so labour stays unused in one place while needs go unmet elsewhere.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: The consequences of market failure are misallocation: goods with external costs and demerit goods tend to be over-consumed, drawing more resources than their full effects justify, while goods with external benefits and merit goods tend to be under-consumed, leaving needs unmet that the same resources could serve.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: An Oshakati clinic sells flu vaccinations at N$60 and 300 are bought in a season, though the level serving the whole town - counting the protection each vaccinated person gives to others - is nearer 900, so the market falls 600 vaccinations short, since 900 - 300 = 600 vaccinations.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.
